newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla faces grand jury probe.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla faces grand jury probe.

text.p: California juice maker Odwalla Inc. said Thursday that it faces a federal grand jury probe connected with last year's outbreak of bacterial sickness that was linked to its apple juice.

"The company has been informed that it is the subject of a federal grand jury investigation concerning events of 1996 and before, including the e.coli 0157:h7 incident," the Half Moon Bay, Calif.-based company said in a statement accompanying its earnings report. "The company has responded to a subpoena and is cooperating fully with the government."

Last fall, Odwalla recalled 13 juice products after its apple juice was implicated in an outbreak of E.coli bacteria. More than 40 people were taken ill from bacterial poisoning, including a 16-month-old girl who later died.
Odwalla said it could not predict the outcome of the investigation.
The company also said that of nine lawsuits filed against it, five had been settled, including one class action suit. It did not give details of the settlement.

The company reported a net loss of $1.8 million, or 36 cents a share for its fiscal third quarter ended May 31. That compared with a profit of $522,000, or 10 cents a share, a year earlier. Sales fell 17 percent to $13.7 million from $16.5 million.
